89d66ea: Bug in credential redaction (gflo/observe.py redact_text, used by redact_json for public artifacts and the worker trace): credentials inside JSON that was itself embedded in a message are escaped once per nesting level, e.g. {"evidence": "token=\"ALPHA BETA\""} serialised again several times. Assignments of api_key/apikey/api-key, password, secret and token whose key or value quotes are backslash-escaped at any depth must have their whole value replaced by [redacted]: a quoted value ends only at a closing quote with the same escape depth as its opening quote (an escaped quote inside the value has a different depth), single and double quotes both count, an unterminated quoted value is hidden through the end of the text, and unquoted values end at whitespace, comma, quote or }. The input object must never be modified. The worker's private trace must redact a previous attempt's review evidence such as token="ALPHA BETA", while the request sent to the model keeps the previous verdict unchanged. Add regression tests.
0c9c7c8: Bug in gflo/artifacts.py unpack_archive(stream, destination, limits): the entry limit (limits.entries) counts only archive members, so an archive with a single member 'a/b/c/file' creates three implicit parent directories and bypasses the limit. Count every filesystem node the extraction would create (each member plus all of its parent directories, deduplicated) and reject with a ValueError mentioning the 'filesystem entry limit' before anything is extracted; the destination must not exist after the rejection. Add regression tests.
6dd3556: Robustness bug in gflo/environment.py EnvironmentStore: (1) a reader can resolve a receipt while a publication is in progress; resolve must take the store lock in shared mode (locked(shared=True)) while publish keeps it exclusive, so a resolve attempted from inside an in-progress publication is refused with the existing 'Another environment preparation owns this store' error; internal calls made while publish already holds the lock must use a lock-free _resolve. (2) If publish fails after renaming the staged directory to its receipt id (for example the directory fsync raises OSError), the new publication must be retired by renaming it back to the private staging path before the error propagates, so only previously published receipts remain addressable and still resolve. Add regression tests.
edc7d71: Bug in gflo/environment.py EnvironmentStore.publish(stream, metadata, verify, cancelled=...): cancellation is not checked at the final commit boundary. After the published directory is durable and re-resolved, check cancellation once more immediately before the final commit step; if cancelled, raise the existing ValueError mentioning cancellation and leave the candidate unpublished (only previously published receipt ids remain), while cleanup after a successful commit must never remove the committed publication. Add regression tests.
6ea52be: Bug in gflo/environment.py EnvironmentStore.publish: if publication fails after the staged directory was renamed to its receipt id and retiring it (renaming it back) also fails, the failed candidate stays addressable and resolve() accepts it. Write a durable 'pending' marker file into the staging directory (fsync the file and the directory) before renaming it into place, remove the marker only as the final commit step after the published environment resolves, and make resolve refuse any environment whose 'pending' marker exists with a ValueError mentioning 'pending' (the publish path itself may resolve while pending). Previously published environments keep resolving. Add regression tests.
